blocks.text: When building models, it is important to consider the ethical implications, such as fairness and privacy.
A model should be fair and not biased. For example, if a model is used to decide who gets a loan, it should not unfairly favor one group of people over another.

When using personal data to build models, it is important to respect privacy. For example, if a company is using customer data to build models, they should ensure the data is secure and not shared without permission.

blocks.title: Tidbits
blocks.text: Always visualize your data before building models and test your results on new data for better accuracy.

You are given the following data that shows the relationship between the number of hours studied and the marks obtained in a test by students. Your task is to build a linear regression model that predicts the marks based on the number of hours studied.

items: Plot the data points on a graph (Hours studied on the x-axis and Marks obtained on the y-axis).
Calculate the equation of the line using linear regression.
Use the equation to predict the marks for a student who studied for 7 hours.
How well does the model fit the data? Justify your answer by calculating the error between actual and predicted marks.

blocks.text: You are a college administrator, and you want to predict whether students will pass or fail a final exam based on their midterm marks. The following data shows the midterm marks of students and whether they passed or failed the final exam. Your task is to build a logistic regression model to predict the likelihood of passing based on midterm marks.

blocks.caption: Midterm marks and final exam result

items: Plot the data points (Midterm marks on the x-axis, and Pass/Fail on the y-axis).
Fit a logistic regression model to the data.
Based on the model, predict the probability of passing for a student who scored 55 in the midterm.
Discuss how the logistic regression model helps in making this prediction and whether it's accurate.

blocks.text: You work in a local retail shop, and you want to segment your customers into two groups based on their monthly spending in two categories: groceries and clothing. The following table shows the monthly spending of six customers. Your task is to use K-means clustering to group these customers into two clusters based on their spending habits.

items: Choose K = 2 clusters and randomly select two initial cluster centers.
Assign each customer to the nearest cluster based on their spending.
Recalculate the cluster centers by finding the average spending in each category for each cluster.
Repeat the process until the cluster centers stabilize.
Analyze the clusters and describe the spending habits of customers in each group.
